raw_response:
I will start from what worked for me last year and only adjust a little. On my 7.5 mu, I cannot gamble. Fertilizer costs real money, but losing yield costs more, so I will not cut too hard on base fertilizer, especially for cabbage, chili, and eggplant because these three take a lot out of the soil and the marketable yield depends on strong early growth. I have well irrigation, so I will water on time instead of waiting for the sky. Around Quzhou, if cabbage and chili are short of water or fertilizer at the wrong stage, the field shows it fast and the income drops fast too. I will keep cabbage on the stronger land with more farmyard manure and compound fertilizer, chili and eggplant on land that drains better, kidneybean lighter because too much nitrogen makes vines run, and maize steady and cheaper because it is less delicate. I do listen to dealers and village trainings some, but I still look most at what has held up in nearby fields. This year I will use hybrid seed for chili, eggplant, maize, and most cabbage because the stand is more even and yield is safer. For kidneybean I will stay with improved seed, not push too much nitrogen, and focus on clean emergence, two or three irrigations, and timely spraying. I will plough before the season, then rotary where I need a fine seedbed for vegetables.
